[DSC turned a 10-terabyte national voter file, delivered as thousands of inconsistent state files, into a resource researchers across campus now use directly.]{.lede}

DSC piloted **Redivis**, a secure platform for restricted research data, backed for its
first two years by University Librarian discretionary funds. It's since become a
sustained subscription, paid from the Archive's operating fund alongside <abbr class="term" title="Inter-university
Consortium for Political and Social Research">ICPSR</abbr> and Roper. The platform
holds about {{< var redivis.data_volume >}} of <abbr class="term" title="Data
protection levels covering FERPA, PII, and HIPAA-regulated research data">P3/P4-compliant</abbr>
data across {{< var redivis.users >}} registered users and over {{< var redivis.workflows >}}
workflows. Piloted in 2022 and run as a governed service since January 2023, it has
processed **{{< var redivis.petabytes_processed >}}** in total through 2025, 2.9 PB of that in
2024 alone.

The flagship dataset is the **L2 historic voter file**, over 10TB of national voter
history purchased by DSC and a Library subject selector. It arrived as thousands of
fragmented, state-level files, too large to store locally and too inconsistent to
analyze as-is. DSC consolidated it into a single, version-controlled,
analysis-ready dataset, cited by Redivis's own CEO as a flagship use case at FORCE11
2024.

Researchers use it directly across departments: election administration (Joshua
Ferrer, Political Science), gentrification patterns (Alexandria Davis, Political
Science), population behavior and public policy (Economics), and a project merging
the voter file with UCLA medical records to study health and voting (Straus,
Thompson, Vavreck, Naeim, UCLA Health). As the graduate student who curated the
dataset put it:

> *"Professors and students in a social sciences department are able to instantly work with a large, rich dataset in a secure environment."*
> — Graham Straus, UCLA Political Science PhD student, FORCE11 2024
